subject: Performance SLO qualification & benchmark methodology exchange
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@edgefin.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Feb 2027 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: Performance SLO targets & next steps

Hi Sarah \u0014 thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on the benchmark scope and timeline.

Key targets you called out on the call:
- Latency: p95 <= 180-200ms for short responses (~<128 tokens); p95 <= 500ms for 512-token completions (interactive requirements).
- Throughput: sustained 120 req/s for the primary workload (50% short chat, 30% single turn long responses, 20% embeddings/re-ranking).
- Concurrency: target ability to support concurrency of ~40-50 simultaneous active sessions with steady-state tail latency SLAs.
- Streaming: must support token-level streaming with first-byte latency <50ms for partial results (important for your UI).
- Quality: no measurable drop vs. your current baseline prompts (we'll run quality regression checks using your eval set).

Benchmark scope we propose:
1) Reproducible harness run using Redwood benchmark runner (we provide container + config).
2) Prompt sets: you mentioned sending a sample; we'll run across dev/qa/prod-sized sets.
3) Measurement definitions: p50/p90/p95/p99 for both first-byte and final-token latencies, throughput and error rates, concurrency stress runs, and streaming-first-byte timings.
4) Repro steps and seeds for determinism on model runs where feasible.

Next steps / requests:
- Can you share a representative prompt set (or 200-500 sample prompts) for the different workload buckets? Prefer JSONL with metadata tags (intent/len).
- Any constraints on data residency or input sanitization for the test artifacts?
- We'll draft a short SLO test plan and share measurement definitions; once you sign off we'll schedule a 4-hour dedicated run slot on Redwood Dedicated.

I've attached a short proposal with suggested test matrix and timeline (redwood-benchmark-proposal.xlsx). I copied Rishi to help coordinate infra.

If this looks right, will send a formal test plan and a proposed calendar slot for next week.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachment: redwood-benchmark-proposal.xlsx (spreadsheet: proposed test matrix and timeline)

From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tomas Novak <tomas@edgefin.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Feb 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLO targets & next steps

Marissa \u0014 thanks for the write-up, that's a good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: our product team wants to prioritize the interactive scenario. Please use p95 180ms for responses under 128 tokens as the primary bar. For longer generations (up to 512 tokens) p95 of 500ms is acceptable.
- Concurrency: our expected peak is 50 concurrent active sessions (mostly short-chat with occasional long completions).
- Throughput: 120 req/s sustained is correct as a baseline; we may test up to 200 req/s in a spike run.
- Streaming: yes, streaming support is required. We need partial token latency (first-byte) to be low; target <50ms when possible.
- Quality/regression: we will provide a small eval harness and expected pass/fail thresholds for intent/slot accuracy and hallucination checks.

I've attached a first-pass sample prompt set (edgefin_prompts_v1.jsonl) \u0014 ~300 items across intents and lengths. Sensitive data has been stubbed. We're ok with you using a staging copy of our data for the run; legal will confirm.

Can you also include your measurement definitions (how you compute p95 over streaming-first-byte vs final-token) and the reproducibility steps (seed usage, fixed model versions)? That will help our engineering team sign the plan.

Thanks,

Sarah Liu
Senior Product Manager, EdgeFin
sarah.liu@edgefin.com

Attachment: edgefin_prompts_v1.jsonl (sample prompts, 300 items)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@edgefin.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Feb 2027 13:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification & benchmark methodology exchange

Sarah \u0014 great, thanks for the prompt set. I attached a short SLO test plan and measurement definitions that map directly to the bullets you and your engineers called out. Highlights below and in the attached slo-test-plan.md: 

Measurement definitions (short):
- First-byte latency (streaming): measure time from request ingress to when the first partial token is returned to the client. Compute p50/p90/p95/p99 across the run window.
- Final-token latency: measure time from request ingress to completion (all tokens). Same percentile breakdown.
- Throughput: measured as successful completions/sec over sliding 1-minute windows; report sustained and spike windows.
- Error rate: percent of requests with non-200s or timeouts (>10s).
- Concurrency: measured by number of active requests with an open stream/socket. We will run linear ramp tests to characterize tail-latency behavior as concurrency increases.

Reproducibility & harness:
- We'll provide a Dockerized benchmark runner (link below) and a pinned hash for the container/image. Runs are parameterized by model-version, prompt-seed, and concurrency schedule.
- Determinism: where the model supports a seed we set fixed seeds for generation; for streaming/tokens some variance is expected, so we report confidence intervals and run 3 repeats for each cell in the matrix.
- Data: we'll run on the sample JSONL you provided; any sensitive strings will be flagged and redacted \u0014 thanks for stubbing.

Links / artifacts: 
- Benchmark harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-harness/tree/edgefin-run-2027
- Shared drive with test artifacts and results template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cEdgeFin-benchmark

Proposed schedule: 
- Sign-off on test plan by EOD Friday (Feb 5)
- Dedicated 4-hour run window week of Feb 8 (we'll reserve Redwood Dedicated for the slot)
- Results + regression analysis delivered within 48 hours of run completion

Attachments: slo-test-plan.md (measurement definitions, run matrix)

Connor & Rishi \u0014 can you confirm infra availability and whether we need any special provisioning (reserved GPUs, network egress rules) for the run?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: slo-test-plan.md (markdown: definitions and run matrix)

Quick update \u0014 allocated a dedicated run slot on Redwood Dedicated for Feb 9, 0800-1200 PST, and reserved the required GPU pool. Network and egress: we'll use the customer-approved VPC peering for data ingress; legal can confirm.

Infra notes for the run:
- We'll provision a cluster sized to meet 200 req/s spike and sustained 120 req/s baseline with target concurrency 50 to exercise tail behavior.
- The benchmark runner will be deployed in an isolated tenant on the dedicated pool; we will capture per-token traces and the streaming first-byte timestamps as defined in the slo-test-plan.md.
- We'll take three repeats per matrix cell and publish raw traces + aggregated percentiles to the shared Drive link after the run.

Sarah \u0014 please confirm the Feb 9 slot works for your team and that the sample prompts are final. Once you confirm, I'll set up the runbook and invite the run leads.

Connor Obrien
